entries.value: Charles Heidsieck Réserve Brut is a Reims Champagne of Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Meunier, roughly a third of each, with about 40 percent reserve wines, aged in the chalk cellars dug beneath the city and at least three years on its lees. It is rich and toasty: roasted nuts, brioche, dried apricot and a creamy texture, dry, with a long finish. Its toastiness suits roasted and nutty flavours. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a tulip or white-wine glass, a touch warmer so its richness shows. Its founder, Charles-Camille Heidsieck, called Champagne Charlie, was arrested in Union-occupied New Orleans in 1862 and held at Fort Jackson.
entries.reason: Five-star review of the description: it opened on the founder, not the wine, and named the Creole Spiced Nuts, the Turtle Soup, the Cheese Board and the Pecan Gulf Fish, none of whose pairings names this wine; it now opens on the wine, speaks of the flavours its goesWith names and carries the founder's New Orleans story

entries.value: Bollinger Special Cuvée is the house Brut from Aÿ, the Grand Cru village known for Pinot Noir: about 60 percent Pinot Noir with Chardonnay and a little Meunier, part fermented in old oak, with reserve wines kept in magnum. It is rich and structured: baked apple, toasted nuts, spice and a firm, dry finish. It is our classic bottle for the Turtle Soup, its toasty style echoing the aged sherry. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a tulip or white-wine glass, so the Pinot Noir shows. It has been James Bond's Champagne since Live and Let Die in 1973, a film shot partly in the French Quarter.

entries.value: Armand de Brignac Brut Gold is a prestige Champagne made at Chigny-les-Roses, blending Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Meunier from three harvests. At disgorgement it takes still wine aged a year in French oak, and it rests 119 steps underground in deep chalk cellars. It is ripe and generous: white peach, brioche and honey with a soft, creamy mousse, made for the big celebration at the table. We ice it early, since the metallic bottle chills slowly, and pour at 45 to 48°F in a tulip or white-wine glass. Guests call it the Ace of Spades, for the pewter emblem on its gold bottle, first released in 2006.
entries.reason: Five-star review of the description: it opened on the brand and the family, not the wine, and named the Turtle Soup, the Louisiana BBQ Lobster and the Cheese Board, none of whose pairings names this wine; it now opens on the wine, speaks of the occasion its goesWith names and keeps the sourced facts

entries.value: Pol Roger Blanc de Blancs 2015 is a vintage Champagne made only from Grand Cru Chardonnay of the Côte des Blancs, from villages such as Cramant, Avize and Oger. It is fermented in steel, village by village, and aged six years in Épernay. It tastes of lemon, white flowers and chalk, with a fine mousse and a long, precise finish. It is our celebration bottle for the Poussin à la Moutarde, cutting the fried crust and mustard cream. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a tulip or white-wine glass, turning the bottle as we ease the cork. Winston Churchill first tasted Pol Roger in 1908.

entries.value: Bollinger PN TX20 is all Pinot Noir, a Blanc de Noirs, its lead village Tauxières, on the Montagne de Reims. PN marks the Pinot Noir range, TX the lead village and 20 the 2020 harvest it is built on, with older reserve wines. It is full and powerful: red apple, white peach, a chalky tension and a long, firm finish. It is our celebration bottle for the Louisiana Oysters, its weight standing up to the barbecue sauce. We pour it at 46 to 50°F in a white-wine glass, warmer than the house bubbles. Lily Bollinger ran the family house in Aÿ from 1941 and doubled its production.

entries.value: Bollinger La Grande Année 2015 is the vintage Champagne of the family house in Aÿ, made only from a harvest it judges great: 60 percent Pinot Noir and 40 percent Chardonnay from eleven villages. It is fermented in oak barrels and aged under natural cork for more than twice the time the rules require. It is rich and layered: baked apple, hazelnut, honey and spice, held by firm acidity and a long finish. That acidity suits crawfish and rich pastry. We pour it at 46 to 50°F in a white-wine glass, warmer than the house bubbles. Queen Victoria granted the house its Royal Warrant in 1884.

entries.value: Jacques Selosse Initial is a Blanc de Blancs from Avize on the Côte des Blancs, all Grand Cru Chardonnay from Avize, Cramant and Oger, blended from three harvests. It is fermented and aged in oak barrels, the way Burgundy makes white wine. It is intense and vinous: ripe citrus, hazelnut, honey and a salty, mineral grip, with vivid acidity. That acidity and salt suit sharp, salty plates. We pour it at 48 to 52°F in a white-wine glass, never a flute, and lift it from the ice if it closes up. The estate dates from 1949, and its way with oak inspired a generation of Champagne growers.

entries.value: Krug Grande Cuvée 170th Edition is a prestige Champagne from Reims, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Meunier, blending 195 wines from twelve years, from 1998 to 2014. Each wine is first fermented in small oak casks, and the blend rests about seven years in the cellars. It is deep and layered: honey, toasted nuts, brioche and citrus peel, with fine bubbles and a very long finish. It suits roasted nuts and grand plates. We pour it at 48 to 52°F in a white-wine glass, warmer than the house bubbles. Joseph Krug founded the house in 1843, set on making a prestige Champagne every year, whatever the harvest.
